sentences.text: ORDER 1.

Appellants have filed this first appeal under Section 74 of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 against the impugned award dated 10.5.2024 passed in MJC-LA No.17/2022 by the Presiding Officer, Dewas, whereby the amount of compensation has been enhanced.

sentences.text: 2. Since there is a delay in filing this appeal, therefore, an application for condonation of delay under Section 5 of Limitation Act is filed.
This appeal is barred by 157 days.

3. Learned counsel appearing for the respondent opposes the aforesaid application on the ground that the delay beyond 120 days cannot be condoned, therefore, this application is not maintainable and liable to be dismissed and the appeal be also dismissed.

sentences.text: 1 Provided that the High Court may, if it is satisfied that the appellant was prevented by sufficient cause from filing the appeal within the said period, allow it to be filed within a further period not exceeding sixty days.

( 2 ) Every appeal referred to under sub-section (1) shall be heard as expeditiously as possible and endeavour shall be made to dispose of such appeal within six months from the date on which the appeal is presented to the High Court.

Explanation.--For the purposes of this section, "High Court"
means the High Court within the jurisdiction of which the land acquired or proposed to be acquired is situated."
5. Under sub-section (1) the appeal lies to the High Court within sixty days from the date of the award and as per proviso the High Court, if satisfied that the appellant was prevented by sufficient cause from filing the appeal within the said period, allow it to be filed within a further period not exceeding sixty days.
Therefore, the original period of limitation is 60 days and which is liable to be extended up to 60 days on sufficient cause.
Therefore, the learned counsel appearing for the respondent is right in objecting this application.
Admittedly this appeal is barred by 120 days and the High Court lacks jurisdiction to condone the delay beyond 120 days.

6. The Apex Court in the case of Chintels India Limited Vs. Bhayana Builders Private Limited report in (2021) 4 SCC 602 has held as under:-
"11.

sentences.text: A reading of section 34(1) would make it clear that an application made to set aside an award has to be in accordance with both sub-sections (2) and (3).

This would mean that such NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:3333 3 FA-2379-2024 application would not only have to be within the limitation period prescribed by sub-section (3), but would then have to set out grounds under sub-sections (2)
and/or (2-A) for setting aside such award.

What follows from this is that the application itself must be within time, and if not within a period of three months,
must be accompanied with an application for condonation of delay, provided it is within a further period of 30 days, this Court having made it clear that section 5 of the Limitation Act, 1963 does not apply and that any delay beyond 120 days cannot be condoned - see State of Himachal Pradesh v. Himachal Techno Engineers and Anr.
(2010) 12 SCC 210 at paragraph 5."
7.

Resultantly the appeal is also dismissed.
